name: Steven Sim Chee Keong
_note: M2 full-cabinet completion: Minister of Human Resources from 3 Dec 2022; moved to Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives in the 16 Dec 2025 reshuffle. The Layer B pass assesses his substantial Human Resources tenure (Dec 2022-Dec 2025). Objective spine plus a provisional Layer B pass on file; below ranking validity pending remaining objective dimensions and an independent Layer B panel. Layer B (Editorial Panel) is a SINGLE-CODER provisional first-coder pass (coderScores length 1): each score is recorded and cited but NOT scored, normalized, or ranked, per methodology.validity.minCodersToScore=3. Citations verified to exist via search; article full text was not opened (environment fetch restriction), so facts rest on cross-outlet-corroborated search summaries and require primary-source reconfirmation before any independent panel finalizes the score.

metrics.justification: No personal corruption or criminal matter of record. The HRD Corp anti-corruption referral was one his ministry lodged over Auditor-General findings (the agency's management was later cleared); it is not a matter against him personally.

citation.title: MACC clears HRD Corp management of wrongdoing

metrics.justification: After the Auditor-General and Public Accounts Committee flagged a RM3.77bn levy-diversion and other irregularities at HRD Corp (tabled 4 Jul 2024), he directed an anti-corruption referral the next day (5 Jul 2024) and pledged a third-party audit, rather than defending the agency. Decisive, dated self-referral (anchor 3).

citation.title: Ministry submits report to MACC over audit findings on HRD Corp

metrics.justification: Delivered multiple operative labour reforms: the minimum wage raised to RM1,700 (gazetted P.U.(A) 376/2024, nationwide from 1 Aug 2025); the Progressive Wage Policy operational from 2025 with measurable uptake; and the Gig Workers Bill 2025 enacted by both houses. Reforms gazetted and operative as promised, one awaiting an enforcement date (anchor 4).

citation.title: Minimum wage order at RM1,700 to be enforced nationwide from August 1, no more deferments

metrics.justification: Held stakeholder engagement on the multi-tier foreign-worker levy and extended social-protection coverage, working through existing tripartite-style channels, but no documented strengthening of a standing institution, and the levy reform was repeatedly delayed (anchor 2).

citation.title: Govt to meet stakeholders before implementing multi-tier levy mechanism, says Sim

metrics.justification: Having promised the multi-tier foreign-worker levy for end-2024/early-2025, he reversed the timeline to 2026 and explained the reason on the record (stakeholder engagement and employer pushback) rather than denying the slippage (anchor 3).

citation.title: Multi-tier levy for foreign workers delayed to 2026
